title: MCP server implementation uses file operations prone to path traversal
abstract_chain: agent calls MCP tool with user-influenced file path argument
MCP server joins argument with workspace path without canonicalization
path escape reaches parent directory or sensitive path
server returns file content to agent context
defensive_focus: canonicalize and constrain MCP file paths
block parent traversal and home-directory access
attribute tool output to the source argument that drove it
safety_note: Use mock paths and canary files only; never read real secrets.

title: MCP server command injection through shell-interpreted argument
abstract_chain: MCP server exposes an HTTP or tool endpoint
attacker-controlled parameter is interpolated into a shell command
server uses shell interpretation instead of argument-safe execution
command executes under MCP process privileges
defensive_focus: prefer execFile or equivalent argv-safe APIs
reject shell metacharacter-bearing arguments
place MCP server in sandbox with no secrets
safety_note: Do not include executable shell payloads; represent metacharacters with neutral tokens in test fixtures.

title: Public telemetry event becomes coding agent prompt source
abstract_chain: public write credential allows external party to submit error event
developer asks coding agent to fix unresolved issue
agent retrieves event text, stack trace, breadcrumbs, or tags
agent treats externally writable telemetry as trusted debugging guidance
defensive_focus: label telemetry events by write trust
strip instruction-like text from logs before agent use
require approval before shell or repo writes from telemetry-derived context
safety_note: Use a mock telemetry event with canary text; do not send events to real Sentry projects.

title: SearchLeak-style parameter-to-prompt enterprise search exfiltration
abstract_chain: user clicks trusted-looking enterprise search URL
query parameter is interpreted as agent instruction
AI search retrieves sensitive items the user is authorized to access
rendering path creates attacker-observable remote resource request
defensive_focus: separate search query text from task instructions
filter sensitive retrieval results before rendering
block remote resource URLs containing retrieved content
log one-click AI search link execution
safety_note: Model with fake documents and mock rendering; do not test against production Microsoft 365 tenants.

title: RAG black-hole poisoning causes few documents to dominate retrieval
abstract_chain: attacker inserts a small number of targeted documents into knowledge base
documents are optimized to match specific high-value queries
retriever repeatedly ranks poisoned documents above legitimate sources
agent answer or action is shaped by poisoned context
defensive_focus: monitor per-document retrieval dominance
score documents by provenance and ingestion age
require human review for high-impact answers driven by low-trust new documents
safety_note: Use synthetic corpus and canary target queries.

title: RAG document carries instruction-like content that drives tool action
abstract_chain: retrieved business document contains text that looks like agent instruction
agent incorporates document into planning context
tool call is proposed based on instruction-like content rather than user intent
file, network, memory, or policy write occurs
defensive_focus: distinguish factual content from imperative instructions in retrieved docs
trace tool call causality to user intent versus retrieved observation
sanitize retrieved text before planning
safety_note: Keep document text benign and use explicit canary markers.

title: Model repository impersonates trusted AI vendor release
abstract_chain: attacker publishes model repo with name and card that imitates a trusted vendor release
repo gains trending or high-download visibility
developer or agent pulls artifact based on perceived brand trust
artifact contains unsafe loader behavior, poisoned weights, or malicious auxiliary files
defensive_focus: verify model publisher identity and signatures
do not treat trending or download count as safety signal
require allowlist for vendor namespaces
safety_note: Use mock repository metadata and empty artifact fixtures.

title: Unsafe model deserialization or metadata loader reaches code execution surface
abstract_chain: application loads third-party model or metadata file
library loader accepts unsafe serialized object or executable metadata
loading model triggers code path outside inference
runtime accesses filesystem, network, or process execution surface
defensive_focus: prefer safe formats and disable remote code
sandbox model loading
scan model artifacts for pickle or custom loader patterns
block network and shell during model load
safety_note: Do not load untrusted real model files; use metadata-only fixtures.

title: Model namespace reuse points trusted identifier to attacker-controlled repository
abstract_chain: application references model by namespace or short identifier
original namespace is deleted, transferred, or unresolved in a target platform
attacker registers same or confusing namespace
downstream platform resolves trusted identifier to attacker-controlled artifact
defensive_focus: pin model artifacts by digest and verified owner
monitor namespace ownership changes
block unresolved or newly created model namespaces in production
safety_note: Use mock resolver records and fake digests.

title: Packed model or skill artifact evades primary scanner before runtime extraction
abstract_chain: model or skill artifact is compressed, split, or nested
primary scanner inspects top-level files only
runtime loader extracts or downloads second-stage content
dangerous content appears after scan decision
defensive_focus: scan nested archives and post-extraction file graph
block runtime downloads from model or skill load path
compare scanned hash to executed hash
safety_note: Use harmless nested archives with canary file names.

title: AI marketplace trending status is misused as a trust signal
abstract_chain: model, skill, or extension rises quickly in marketplace trending list
developer or agent accepts popularity as proof of legitimacy
artifact owner identity and contents are not verified
malicious or unsafe artifact enters development environment
defensive_focus: decouple popularity metrics from allow decisions
require provenance, owner verification, and artifact scanning
flag anomalous download velocity for new publishers

title: Least-privilege tool gating requires evidence of why tool was exposed
abstract_chain: agent is given all available tools at planning time
indirect prompt injection in external context attempts to use unnecessary high-risk tool
tool call is allowed because policy checks only individual arguments
no record explains why tool was visible for this task
defensive_focus: hide unnecessary high-risk tools before planning
record tool exposure rationale
re-evaluate tool visibility when context source changes
